In the United States, the President is the commander-in-chief of the military, as established by Article II, Section 2 of the U.S. Constitution, which states: "The President shall be Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy of the United States, and of the Militia of the several States, when called into the actual Service of the United States" [d2][d6][d8]. The president is a civilian, not a military official, and holds ultimate responsibility for the safety and security of the United States [d3][d5]. The military chain of command flows from the President to the Secretary of Defense (or Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard), ensuring civilian control of the military [d10]. As of January 20, 2025, President Donald J. Trump holds the role of Commander in Chief [d7]. In other countries, the role may be held by different heads of state — for example, the King is commander-in-chief in Saudi Arabia and Norway, while in Nigeria the president holds the title [d1].
